feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 3 (lead 0.05 m, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, 0.6 kg, body 0.12 x 0.10 m, track 0.10 m, kd 0.6) is the best result so far at 493.2. It cut s-bend line loss to 0 and lifted s-bend progress to 0.75, and it gave an oval finish rate of 0.85. The remaining failure is the slalom: 0 of 20 finishes, progress 0.34, line loss 0.35, max_error 0.0624. The Integrator's controller is unchanged from iteration 3 so the track change can be read alone. Read the next race as follows. If slalom progress rises above 0.34 and its off-track ends fall with line loss near 0, keep the 0.08 m track and then test sensor reach. If slalom line loss stays at 0.3 or more with max_error still at or above 0.06 m, the outer sensors are losing the tape at the edge. Then widen to +/-0.07 m with 16 mm footprints, which iteration 1 and iteration 2 evidence supports. If steering_oscillation on the s-bend rises above about 0.5 (iteration 3 measured 0.44) and the slalom does not improve, the sharper turn is overshooting. Then the controller's kp should come down (the Integrator would make that change), and the geometry should go back to the 0.10 m track.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events stay at 0.3 or more and max_error stays at or above 0.06 m, widen the outer sensors to x = +/-0.07 m with 7 sensors and 16 mm footprints, since iteration 1 showed line loss near a 0.0565 m offset and the 0.06 m off-track floor cannot be moved by body width.

If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.5 (iteration 3: 0.44) without a slalom gain, step wheel_track back to 0.09 m rather than going further below 0.08 m, since the sharper turn is overshooting.

If the slalom still fails with line loss at 0 and max_error near 0.06 m, try mass 0.5 kg with the 0.08 m track, since iteration 3 showed that lowering yaw inertia from 0.8 to 0.6 kg (with the lead restored) restored s-bend progress from 0.04 to 0.75.
